messages:
alex: Heads up — ran into a weird case where a helm helper that "splat"-renders a map ends up producing an empty map that kustomize later prunes, so our namespace/labels patch disappears in staging and chart-testing CI fails. Anyone seen this pattern? :confused:

chart-ci-bot: ct --lint --chart-repo . --charts ./charts/myservice
ERROR: rendered manifests contain no resources for patch target: patch: metadata.name: required field missing
(helm template produced no metadata.name for the kustomize target)

maria: ugh, yeah. I saw something similar last month when we moved to stricter values.schema.json. Usually it's because the helper returns nil/empty and the top-level key gets omitted in the final manifest.

sanjay: can you paste the helper and the values snippet?

alex: sure — simplified version:
```
# templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "mychart.renderLabels" -}}
{{- $labels := .Values.baseLabels | merge .Values.extraLabels -}}
labels:
{{ toYaml $labels | nindent 2 }}
{{- end -}}

# values.yaml
baseLabels: null
extraLabels: {}
```
When baseLabels is null, the helper `merge` seems to return null and the whole `labels:` block is dropped. If baseLabels is `{}` it works. helm template in CI sometimes coerces null -> <no value>.

jen: yep. Two quick fixes: 1) ensure defaults in values.yaml / values.schema.json so the key is always an object, or 2) guard in the helper with `default (dict) .Values.baseLabels`. I prefer fixing the helper since it protects callers.

maria: example guard:
```
{{- $base := default (dict) .Values.baseLabels -}}
{{- $extra := default (dict) .Values.extraLabels -}}
{{- $merged := merge $base $extra -}}
labels:
{{ toYaml $merged | nindent 2 }}
```
That ensures an empty map instead of nil and kustomize won't prune the block.

sanjay: another angle — values.schema.json can mask this during ct because `default` in schema isn't applied by helm, but chart-testing might inject defaults. If we add a top-level `properties.baseLabels` with `type: object` and `default: {}`, it helps people using `helm install --set ...` and the schema-based validation will warn.

alex: good call. I tried the helper change locally and it fixes the template output. Still, should we add a small test in ct to catch omitted map sections? Maybe a unit test that runs `helm template` and greps for `labels:` presence for a canonical overlay case.

jen: yes please. Add a tiny smoke test to `.ct.yaml` or GH action: run `helm template` with `--set baseLabels=null` and assert the rendered output still contains `labels:`. That catches regressions from future helper refactors.

maria: one caveat — if an overlay intentionally wants to remove a section, kustomize patching semantics differ. But in our case we always expect labels present for our admission webhooks so they mustn't be pruned. Document this in `charts/README.md` too.

alex: will open a PR with: helper guard + values.schema property + ct smoke test + README note. PR link when ready: https://github.com/redwood/helm-charts/pull/1234 :tada:

sanjay: awesome, thanks. Also add a short comment in the helper about `default (dict)` so future authors know why we coerce null -> {}.

alex: done locally, pushing branch now.

chart-ci-bot: New push to branch "fix/guard-null-labels" — running ct...

jen: nice. once ct passes we can merge and backport to the older chart versions in the release branch.

alex: merging to main after green CI. thanks all :rocket:
